title: The Railroad's Secret
blurb: Silas Kettle has a confession about 1889, and a Burrowing Beetle is tunnelling under your scaffolds. Keep the towers standing while he talks.

objective.text: Keep 5 Scaffold Storeys Standing on Every Cliff

telegram.title: Raise the Towers
telegram.body: BURROWING BEETLE UNDER THE MESA STOP IT BRINGS DOWN SCAFFOLDS FROM BELOW STOP KEEP FIVE STOREYS STANDING ON EVERY CLIFF AT EVERY DAWN STOP LANTERNS FLUSH IT UP EARLY STOP SILAS WISHES TO SPEAK STOP LET HIM

build: stroud
Something's digging under the mesa. Get your scaffolds up: five storeys a cliff, standing at every dawn.
kettle
Captain. Ranchers. I've kept something quiet for eleven years. It's about the tunnel.
stroud
Silas, they're busy. Confess between waves like a gentleman.
wave: Beetles at the walls. Keep those towers standing!

build: kettle
The 1889 blast wasn't an accident. The railroad packed that tunnel on purpose.
kettle
They wanted the canyon cleared of homesteaders. Cheaper than buying them out.
pearl
Silas. You knew? I've been cheating honest people at cards for less.
wave: Ground's shaking. That beetle's coming up under a tower. Lanterns flush it out!

build: kettle
I rigged the charges. They told me it was a mine. They never said what was below it.
kettle
But Granddad's survey did. Josiah knew. He sold them the canyon, and they sold me the dynamite.
kettle
And Pell's Toes? Pell danced a jig at the railhead ball in '72. On both feet. I was there.
stroud
One more night. Then we decide what to do with the truth. And with Silas.
wave: Shoot straight tonight. I owe this canyon that much.

short: Towers are coming down! Rebuild before dawn or the survey's lost.
boss_down: That beetle had my old shovel marks on its back. Good riddance.
win: Towers stood, the beetle's buried, and the railroad's secret is out. Some of it.
Feels lighter. Like dropping an anvil off a cliff. Doesn't make it right.
lost: Not enough timber standing at dawn. Back to the mesa, ranchers.

journal.title: Specimen Notes, No. 5
journal.body:
Silas told me everything tonight. The railroad paid him to blast the tunnel and clear the canyon of homesteaders, and his grandfather's survey told them exactly where.

The thirty-degree law was never about Governor Pell's toes. A law that keeps every barrel off the canyon floor protects only one thing down there: whatever the Board is mining.

- E. Whitlow, Rail Car 9

headline_loss: Mesa Scaffolds Collapse; Beetle Undermines Ranch
